To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

CDP-choline administration partially prevented the changes in the diglyceride pool, in free fatty acids, in the phosphatidycholine labelling and in the phosphatidylinositol labelling found in the brain of gerbils submitted to carotid artery occlusion.
CDP-choline, administered intraperitoneally to gerbils, partially prevents the changes of brain lipid metabolism found in gerbils subjected to carotid ligation.
CDP-choline partially prevented the alterations of lipid metabolism in brain due to ischemia.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the influence of CDP- choline in the lipid metabolism of the gerbil brain during ischemia.
the influence of CDP- choline on lipid metabolism during ischemic conditions.
the influence of CDP-Choline, an agent which has been shown to improve the cerebral blood flow and the cerebral metabolism, on the brain lipid metabolism in a model of cerebral ischemia in gerbils.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the treatment with CDP-choline was effective only in the case of the diglyceride labelling, and that this treatment did not influence the other metabolic parameters studied.
CDP-choline is a useful agent for the prevention of brain damage due to ischemia.

CDP-choline, given before the ischemic insult, prevents the increase of the free arachidonate and the increase of the diglyceride pool, and it also prevents, in part, the decrease of the labelling of phosphatidyl choline, which is due to ischemia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CDP-choline partially corrects the ischemia induced changes of brain lipid metabolism.
the CDP-choline administration partially prevented the changes in brain lipid metabolism found after ischemia.
the administration of CDPcholine to animals submitted to ischemia is effective to partially correct the changes found in brain lipid metabolism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CDP-choline, a phospholipid precursor, can partially restore the changes in brain lipid metabolism caused by ischemia.
CDP-choline can be used to treat ischemic stroke patients.
CDP-choline, a precursor of phosphatidyl-choline, can prevent some of the changes in lipid metabolism induced by ischemia.
